reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses SRO in CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi HEAs, showing SRO affects phase stability and mechanical properties, but it does not address Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles, premelting/melting behavior, or the specific Ni-centered mechanism proposed. The key premises about SRO governing melting in this system are therefore unsupported by the provided passage.
premises: Short-range chemical ordering (SRO) exists in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles and can be tuned by cooling rate.
SRO, especially Ni-centered interactions, raises the energy barrier for atomic rearrangements and increases local cohesive energy.
Loss of SRO upon heating decreases local cohesive energy, triggering premelting below the bulk melting point.
Higher initial SRO leads to delayed, heterogeneous premelting and a broader melting regime compared to randomized nanoparticles.
